scenario: WIBTA for going on a trip my wife can no longer go on because of her DUI? | Last year, my wife and I made plans to spend a week in Montreal with another couple we're close friends with. None of us had been to Canada before, and we thought it would be fun if we all went together. We requested time off work, bought flights, made hotel reservations, etc. The trip is scheduled for March. Here's the problem: a month we made all these arrangements, my wife was arrested for drunk driving, and she pleaded guilty to the charge this week. My understanding is that she can no longer enter Canada with a DUI on her record. But I still want to go on the trip, which I paid a lot of money for, and I told our friends I still plan on accompanying them. My wife and I got into a huge fight over it, and she accused me of being selfish and unsupportive for wanting to go without her. I don't think that's fair. I've supported her throughout the entire court process, which has been incredibly stressful and expensive, and I've been looking forward to this trip for a long time. WIBTA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what to do in this situation. My wife and I planned a trip to Montreal with some close friends. We've been looking forward to it for a while, and we've already spent a lot of money on flights, hotels, and taking time off work. But then, my wife got arrested for DUI and pleaded guilty. Now, she can't go to Canada because of that. I still want to go because I've invested so much time and money into this trip, and I told our friends I would be there. But my wife is upset, saying I'm being selfish and not supportive. I don't think that's fair because I've been there for her through the court process, which was really stressful and expensive. I'm confused about whether I should go or not. What should I do? First, I need to understand the legal aspect. Does a DUI really prevent her from entering Canada? I think Canada has strict entry rules, especially for criminal charges. So, she might not be allowed in. That means she can't go on the trip, but I still want to. Next, I should consider the emotional impact. My wife is going through a tough time with the DUI. She's probably feeling guilty, stressed, and maybe even ashamed. I want to support her, but I also have my own feelings about the trip. It's something we both looked forward to, and now it's falling apart because of her situation. I also need to think about our relationship. We had a huge fight about this. She accused me of being selfish, and I feel like I'm being misunderstood. I've been supportive through the court process, so why is she upset now? Maybe she feels like I'm abandoning her or not considering her feelings. On the other hand, I've invested a lot into this trip. I paid for flights, hotels, and took time off work. It's a significant amount of money, and I don't want to lose that. Plus, I told our friends I would be there, and I don't want to let them down. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can go on the trip but come back early to support her, or maybe she can stay home while I go. But she might feel left out or upset if I leave her alone. I also need to think about the future of our relationship. If I go, will that cause more problems? Or if I stay, will I regret missing the trip? It's a tough spot to be in. I should probably talk to her again, calmly, and try to understand her perspective. Maybe we can find a solution that works for both of us. But I'm not sure how to approach that conversation without it turning into another fight. In the end, I have to decide what's more important: supporting my wife through her tough time or going on the trip that I've been looking forward to. It's a difficult choice, and I wish there was an easy answer.
